text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Interviewed on CNN's World Business Today programme, Danish prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said that he thought it would be beneficial for Denmark to join EMU (Europe's economic and monetary union) in the long run but that Danes would have the final say on participation in a national referendum. Denmark qualifies for EMU but opted out of a single European currency in a referendum in 1993.

--More than 300 dissatisfied investors who lost double-digit million crown sums in bankrupt Danish insurer Hafnia, which collapsed in 1993, see a realistic possibility of getting compensation for their losses, lawyers preparing a test case said. Hafnia was taken over by Codan, leading Den Danske Bank was heavily involved.

--Airlines' passenger bonus programmes represent a hindrance to free competition in the skies, Denmark's Competition Council says, threatening the European Union's deregulation of air traffic. The Council is to analyse point systems and decide whether or not to intervene.

--Denmark's windmill industry is consolidating its leading position on the world market. Danish windmill turbine manufacturers Vestas Wind Systems and Bonus Energy are among firms to win part of a huge Japanese eight billion crown order for 1,000 windmills generating in total 765 megawatts of electricity and due for completion by the year 2003.
